learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.

observations.action: Selected About 40,000 km; Lock it in
observations.outcome: Prediction retained; controls unlocked; instructed to draw 20,000 km ring then move pin.

observations.action: From Madrid 8,000 km ring, clicked Ring at 20,000 km, then Move pin to Wellington; pressed Home on Ring distance
observations.outcome: Ring real length changed 38,059 to 95 km; map recentered Wellington; minimum 1,000 km showed real length 6,257 km. Madrid–Wellington remained 19,855 km. Reveal remained enabled after moving range back.

observations.action: Inspected screenshot of Wellington/20,000 km state
observations.outcome: Dark 1257x936 viewport; circular map, labels, range and readouts legible, lower reveal requires ordinary vertical scrolling. No horizontal cutoff observed.
Not quite: About 20,000 km. Half circumference 20,015 km on a sphere; antipode is unique; map edge stretches that point into a circle; 95 km ring explanation links observed boundary.

prediction.reason: Plausible circumference/half-circumference alternatives support actual commitment.

interaction.reason: Ring and recentering give causal contrasts; lower radius checks a boundary.

payoff.reason: Explains original wrong prediction and tiny boundary ring using explicit sphere model.

clarity.reason: Visible labels and guided two-action unlock were clear in tested desktop view.

transfer.reason: Reusable antipode principle and Madrid–Wellington illustration; no applied new task.

accessibility.reason: Insufficient mode checks; only range Home observed.

surprise.reason: Committed 40,000 prediction reversed by half-circumference and tiny far ring.

visualExplanation.reason: Map edge and ring carry spatial explanation.

playfulness.reason: Radius and pin offer reversible exploration.

practicalValue.reason: Provides geographic distance bound and named city comparison.

depth.reason: Shortest route, antipode and projection edge are linked mechanisms.

complexity.reason: Links shortest surface route, antipode and projected map edge with numeric support.

notationRepresentationBurden.reason: Must reconcile flat circular map edge with single spherical point.

whyCool: Moving the ring to 20,000 km leaves only 95 km of real ring while the map displays a huge circle, and the reveal explains the stretched antipodal edge.

missingEvidence: Phone, contrast, focus sequence, zoom/reflow and motion checks; exhaustive pin/radius states not tested.
